title.zh: 双路径动理学色散关系

summary: Evaluate conventional finite-harmonic and Ronnmark determinants at the same derived equilibrium wavepoint.

capability: Evaluate conventional finite-harmonic and Ronnmark determinants at the same derived equilibrium wavepoint.
operation: evaluate conventional and Ronnmark kinetic determinants
SI equilibrium controls and dimensionless probe ratios to two kinetic dispersion tensors
discovery.boundary: the conventional sum clamps |kz|<1e-10 to +1e-10; Ronnmark keeps zero kz

identity.relation: SI equilibrium controls and dimensionless probe ratios to two kinetic dispersion tensors
identity.direction: SI equilibrium controls and dimensionless probe ratios to two kinetic dispersion tensors
identity.definition: The graph derives omega=omega_frac*wn, kx=kx_frac*kn and f=omega/(2*pi), then evaluates the Weideman sum and Ronnmark paths with shared SI species state.
identity.coordinates: wavevector x-z plane, z parallel to B0; kz is an absolute input
identity.boundary: the conventional sum clamps |kz|<1e-10 to +1e-10; Ronnmark keeps zero kz
assumptions: All species controls describe one shared equilibrium snapshot.

inputs.name: ms
inputs.description: Mass of each species, entering the thermal speed and cyclotron frequency
inputs.constraints: Finite positive masses, one value per species.

inputs.name: qs
inputs.description: Charge of each species, setting the sign of the cyclotron frequency and coupling terms
inputs.constraints: Finite nonzero charges, one value per species.

inputs.name: ns_unit
inputs.description: Density of each species relative to the reference density
inputs.constraints: Finite positive density ratios matching the species axis.

inputs.name: Ts_unit
inputs.description: Temperature of each species relative to the reference temperature
inputs.constraints: Finite positive temperature ratios matching the species axis.

inputs.name: B0
inputs.description: Background magnetic-field strength, setting the cyclotron frequency and entering the pole-resonance argument

inputs.name: n00
inputs.description: Reference number density, converting relative to absolute density

inputs.name: T00
inputs.description: Reference temperature, converting relative to absolute temperature
inputs.constraints: Finite positive reference temperature in eV.

inputs.name: omega_frac
inputs.description: Angular frequency as a multiple of the wn derived internally by this graph (the source implementation writes w=wf(p)*wcn); the caller supplies a dimensionless ratio and this graph derives the absolute angular frequency
inputs.constraints: Finite ratio producing nonzero angular frequency.

inputs.name: kz
inputs.description: Wavevector component parallel to the magnetic field, entering the parallel-resonance argument
inputs.constraints: Finite absolute parallel wavenumber; zero is supported by the kinetic paths.

inputs.name: kx_frac
inputs.description: Perpendicular wavenumber as a multiple of the kn derived internally by this graph (the source implementation writes kx=kxf(p)*kn); the caller supplies a dimensionless ratio and this graph derives the absolute perpendicular wavenumber

inputs.name: lmx
inputs.description: Bessel truncation order for the conventional harmonic sum

outputs.name: scales
outputs.description: Per-species scales derived from the equilibrium inputs, shared by both dispersion paths from the same state snapshot
outputs.units: mixed (each key carries its own unit)
outputs.constraints: The returned value follows the stated shape and physical normalization.

outputs.name: determinant_sum_n
outputs.description: Dispersion determinant of the conventional truncated-harmonic-sum path
outputs.constraints: The returned value follows the stated shape and physical normalization.

outputs.name: determinant_ronnmark
outputs.description: Dispersion determinant of the Ronnmark fast path
outputs.constraints: The returned value follows the stated shape and physical normalization.

outputs.name: K_sum_n
outputs.description: Dielectric tensor of the conventional sum path
outputs.constraints: The returned value follows the stated shape and physical normalization.

outputs.name: D_sum_n
outputs.description: Dispersion tensor of the conventional sum path
outputs.constraints: The returned value follows the stated shape and physical normalization.

outputs.name: K_ronnmark
outputs.description: Dielectric tensor of the Ronnmark path
outputs.constraints: The returned value follows the stated shape and physical normalization.

outputs.name: D_ronnmark
outputs.description: Dispersion tensor of the Ronnmark path
outputs.constraints: The returned value follows the stated shape and physical normalization.

outputs.name: branches
outputs.description: Method-branch label selected for each (species, pole) combination on the Ronnmark path
outputs.constraints: The returned value follows the stated shape and physical normalization.

outputs.name: omega
outputs.description: Absolute angular frequency derived by this graph from omega_frac and the internal wn
outputs.constraints: The returned value follows the stated shape and physical normalization.

outputs.name: kx
outputs.description: Absolute perpendicular wavenumber derived by this graph from kx_frac and the internal kn
outputs.constraints: The returned value follows the stated shape and physical normalization.

outputs.name: f
outputs.description: Frequency converted from the absolute angular frequency
outputs.constraints: The returned value follows the stated shape and physical normalization.

outputs.name: graph_order
outputs.description: Fixed execution-order labels of this graph
outputs.constraints: The returned value follows the stated shape and physical normalization.

preconditions: Species arrays are finite, non-empty and shape-compatible; masses, densities and temperatures are positive, with nonzero charge and magnetic field.
The wavepoint and derived frequency/scales are finite and satisfy the selected numerical path domain.
supported: Evaluate conventional finite-harmonic and Ronnmark determinants at the same derived equilibrium wavepoint.
excluded: Mode identification, root finding and accuracy outside the tested finite-harmonic or rational-pole approximation.
Inputs that violate the numerical domain or require a different tensor convention.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: The first invalid graph control or dependency input raises ValueError; no partial result mapping is returned.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Dependency numerical errors propagate without fallback; solver diagnostics remain observable where returned.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: No graph feedback loop is exposed.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial mapping is returned after an exception.

python.signature: evaluate_kinetic_dispersion_relation(ms, qs, ns_unit, Ts_unit, B0, n00, T00, omega_frac, kz, kx_frac, lmx=5)

example.description: Evaluate both kinetic dispersion paths at one shared derived wavepoint.
example.code:
from scirel.kinetic import evaluate_kinetic_dispersion_relation
r=evaluate_kinetic_dispersion_relation(ms=[9.1094e-31],qs=[-1.60217662e-19],ns_unit=[1],Ts_unit=[1],B0=1,n00=6.075e19,T00=1000,omega_frac=1,kz=1326.1942478795652,kx_frac=1); assert 'determinant_sum_n' in r and 'determinant_ronnmark' in r
example.expected: Observed PASS: the composed graph returns both finite-harmonic and Ronnmark determinants together with their 3x3 K/D tensors and derived omega, kx and f.
